claims.claim: Ottawa opened applications Oct. 15, 2026 for $430 million over five years for skilled trades training, most from an expanded Union Training and Innovation Program launched in 2017
Secretary of State for Labour John Zerucelli announced the funding
Facility and infrastructure expressions of interest close Nov. 12, with shovel-ready projects sought for next spring
Equipment stream applications are ongoing with the federal share temporarily raised to 70 per cent from 50 per cent
Innovation stream proposals are due Dec. 17
Nearly half the $430 million was accounted for in a previous Liberal pledge to spend $8 billion to recruit and train up to 100,000 skilled trades workers over five years
Carney announced Team Canada Strong on April 29, 2026 as a $6 billion five-year plan to recruit, train and hire 80,000 to 100,000 new Red Seal workers
The training component of Team Canada Strong is $331 million over five years from 2026-27 plus $18 million ongoing, including expansion of the Union Training and Innovation Program
The Spring Economic Update 2026 lists a Team Canada Strong target of 80,000 to 100,000 new Red Seal skilled trades workers by 2030-31
The canada.ca release announcing the $430 million was published Oct. 15, 2026 but its page text was not retrievable
The $8 billion figure in the Oct. 15 CP copy and the $6 billion figure in the April PMO release are not reconciled in the sources
No Ontario-specific allocation of the $430 million has been confirmed in the announcement material
The $430 million is a national application-based program open to unions and training providers, with no per-province formula in the sources
